cards.explanation: The answer is Submit to them. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says, “Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities…” It's right at the top of his list, friends, so he isn't whispering it. Nobody gets to skip the first item.
The answer is False. Paul says the believers are to be “…obedient and ready for every good work…” He never gives a convenience clause, friends. No fine print, no small print, nothing.
The answer is no one. That's the whole answer, and it's a big one. Paul says believers are “…to malign no one…” He doesn't leave a list of people who've earned it, friends, and I checked twice.

The answer is peaceable and gentle. Paul says to be “…peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.” Two soft words, friends, and they're aimed at everyone. Not just the people who are easy to be nice to.

The answer is all sorts of desires and pleasures. Paul says we were “…enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures…” Notice the word "we," friends. He's including himself in that group, and I think that's why it lands so gently.

The answer is God's kindness and love. That's what appeared, friends. Paul says, “But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared…” After a list that heavy, the "but" lets you breathe.

The answer is False. Paul writes, “He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy…” So God saved us according to His mercy, friends, and nobody has to pretend they earned it.
The answer is mercy. Paul says God saved us, “…but according to His mercy…” That's what the saving rests on, friends, not on anything we did. I'm glad, because my edges were never going to carry it.
The answer is the Holy Spirit. Paul says God saved us through “…the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.” The renewing is the Spirit's work, friends. Nobody has to do it themselves.

The answer is True. Paul says, “This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior…” Poured out, abundantly, through Jesus. I can't make that sentence any bigger than it already is, friends.
The answer is eternal life. Paul says we would become “…heirs with the hope of eternal life.” And he says we're justified by God's grace, friends, so it's a gift, not a paycheck.

The answer is good deeds. Paul says he wants this stressed “…so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds.” Look who it's for, friends: those who have believed God. Believing and doing good show up in the same sentence, and I'm not about to separate them. I tried that once with a batch, chocolate chips on one side of the counter and dough on the other, and nobody wanted what came out of that oven.

The answer is True. Paul says to avoid “…foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.” He says it plainly, friends. He doesn't soften it, so neither will I.
The answer is two. Paul says to “Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition…” That's a warning, then another warning, and then the decision, friends. It isn't a one-strike thing.

The answer is True. Paul says such a man is “…corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned.” That line comes right after he says to reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition. It's a heavier line in the letter, friends, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously.
The answer is False. Paul says, “…make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.” Winter plans, friends, no courtroom.

The answer is equip. Paul says, “Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.” The goal is that they have everything they need, friends. I like a plan where nobody lacks anything.

The answer is to meet the pressing needs of others. Paul says our people must devote themselves to good works “…in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.” The good works are aimed at the needs in front of them, friends. The focus is on the people in need.
